✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: The wording about line indices is confusing. "from 1 to n" is repeated several times, but it didn't matter in my solution, and as far as I can tell not in your Perl solution either. What matters is printing the number of carts in each line in the original order. I'd drop the indices from the statement and describe lines by position instead ("leftmost", "rightmost", "first", "last"), since indices are an implementation detail.

Suggested wording:
- Each line is indexed from 1 to n. Line i has carts_i shopping carts. => Line i (numbered from left to right) holds carts_i carts.
- If there are multiple such lines, it must be taken from the line with the smallest index. => If there are multiple such lines, take the cart from the leftmost one.
- If there are multiple shortest lines, return the shopping cart to the one with the largest index. => If there are multiple shortest lines, return the cart to the rightmost one.
- Line 2: The initial number of shopping carts carts_i in each shopping cart line from 1 to n, separated by spaces => Line 2: n integers separated by spaces, the initial number of carts carts_i in each line, in left-to-right order.
- Line 1: The number of shopping carts in each line from 1 to n after executing all actions, separated by spaces => Line 1: n integers separated by spaces, the number of carts in each line after all actions, in the same left-to-right order,

Hey CodinGamer! Your contribution has unfortunately not been moderated on time and will temporarily be removed from the system... But no worries! You can republish it anytime to give it another chance! :)
Only 5 hours left to validate. Let's go!

✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: Good easy puzzle. Would make for a great clash but I understand why it isn't one.

General
* I'm confused by the use of two variable names carts_i and c_i throughout the Goal, Input and Constraints sections. Please rename the instances as needed for consistency.

* In both the Goal and Input sections, please change "number of shopping carts" to "initial number of shopping carts" where appropriate, to distinguish it clearly from the resulting number of shopping carts.

Goal
* Tie-breaking for R: the last sentence mentions "take... from" but it should be "return... to".

Constraints
* Please reduce the upper bounds of the following variables to be closer to those used in the cases:

  • [[n]]: 10

  • [[c_i]]: 100

  • length([[actions]]): 100

* Please add: The number of carts returned never exceeds the initial number of carts available.

Optional: Alternatively, instead of adding this constraint, please add a scenario in which a customer attempts to return (R) a cart after all carts have already been taken and returned. In this case, {{IMPOSSIBLE}} should be output.

Stub generator
* Please add a write statement, e.g. "write answer", or "write number of carts or IMPOSSIBLE".

Cases
* Please add a pair of cases where "IMPOSSIBLE" occurs after a number of T and R actions, but *not* on the final action.

* Please add two pairs of cases that clearly test whether a solution handles the tie-breaking rules for take and return operations correctly.

  • In one pair, the final action should be a T operation that requires tie-breaking.

  • In the other pair, the final action should be an R operation that requires tie-breaking.

Thanks.

Changes have been done.

BTW: Returning carts that haven't been taken before is a valid case. It is valid, for example, to let actions start with "R". This is now mentioned as well.

All right, I understand. That works too.

Thank you!
